newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean President Kim backs new labour law.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean President Kim backs new labour law.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Tuesday threw his weight behind a new labour law that has sparked nationwide strikes, saying it was needed to improve the nation's economic competitiveness.

The law "will provide a significant impetus for improved competitiveness", he told a news conference. Labour unions had earlier threatened to escalate industrial action unless Kim announced a repeal of the law.
The new law makes the labour market more flexible by allowing employers to lay off workers, hire temporary staff and replace strikers.
It was rammed through parliament in a dawn session on December 26 with no debate and no opposition deputies present.

"If the Republic is to overcome current economic difficulties, labour and management must establish more productive relations in a spirit of participation and cooperation," Kim said in a prepared statement released in advance of the news conference.
"We should all share the pain of coping with the difficulties facing industry...thus tiding over the current predicament," Kim added.
